articles.title: Ipswich Town's new Buttermarket Planet Blue shop 'here to stay'
articles.summary: Fans and players are delighted at the new "activation space" in the town centre.
articles.body:
Ipswich Town has opened a new shop in the centre of Ipswich as a commitment to the fans and the town, the club says.

The Planet Blue store opened in the Buttermarket shopping centre on Friday with captain Dara O'Shea cutting the ribbon.

It complements the shop at the stadium on Portman Road.

"The football club's the heart of the town and this is right in the middle now, so it's really nice to see," he said.

The opening coincided with the general release of the club's black and gold third kit.

articles.summary: A mass wedding for Palestinian brides and grooms has taken place in the rubble-strewn streets of Gaza.

Amid the ruins of destroyed buildings and displaced people's tents, Gazans gathered to celebrate a mass wedding for Palestinian brides and grooms.

The ceremony, organised by the UAE's humanitarian mission Operation Gallant Knight 3, brought together brides and grooms from across Gaza for a celebration of what organisers described as love and new beginnings in the besieged enclave.

A ceasefire came into force in Gaza in October last year, but Israeli air strikes have continued almost every day.

The Gaza war was triggered by the Hamas-led attack on Israel on 7 October 2023, when about 1,200 people were killed and 251 others were taken hostage.

Israel responded by launching a military campaign against Hamas in Gaza, during which more than 74,640 people have been killed, according to the territory's health ministry.

articles.title: The night-sky image so incredible the NZ man behind it has been accused of using AI
articles.summary: Brendan Larsen spent hours taking hundreds of photographs of the sky over a mountain in New Zealand
articles.body:
A photograph showing thousands of satellites cross-hatching the night sky over New Zealand appeared so extraordinary the astrophotographer who captured it is fighting accusations it was created by AI.

To create his spectacular image – now viewed millions of times online – Brendan Larsen spent two hours in September snapping hundreds of photographs of the night sky over Mount Taranaki in the North Island.

Larsen, 51, says he set his camera up to take an unlimited number of eight-second-long shots, with a two-second gap in between each photo. "I left her running for two hours and captured 578 photos … That was the easy part."

The hard part came next. Larsen spent about 45 hours layering the individual photos – each of which contained about 25 satellites – over one another, using Adobe Photoshop. Much of the time was spent painstakingly erasing stars, to reveal the satellites.

"I could start to see the pattern emerging and realised: 'Wow, this looks really awesome.' I knew if I carried on it would look even better and more impressive in terms of satellite numbers."

The resulting image shows the sky inundated with about 1,400 satellites and 14,000 trails forming a dense crisscrossing pattern above the mountain.

When Larsen uploaded the image to his social media channels in mid-October, it quickly went viral, gaining him 15,000 new followers, clocking up tens of millions of views and igniting thousands of comments.

Some viewers dismissed the photo as AI – but Larsen understands why. "AI generating software is becoming so good it is becoming difficult to tell AI images from real images … especially if you're not familiar with the location or with astrophotography," he says. Still, it is "frustrating".

It is also exasperating, he says, to see his image downloaded and recreated by AI, with obvious flaws.

In anticipation of the AI accusations and backlash, Larsen documented his creative process on video, which he hopes will also allow viewers to form an emotional connection to the landscape.

As a child Larsen was "absolutely blown away" by the number of stars over parts of rural New Zealand. But he has noticed an increase in light pollution and the number of satellites over the six years he has been photographing the sky.

"It's interesting and fascinating seeing satellites, but it's also disturbing," he says.

"I've got about 10,000 comments on my Facebook page … nine out of 10 of the comments are like: 'Wow, beautiful photo, but horrifying, terrifying and really concerning about what's happening to the night sky.'"

About 16,000 working satellites are circling the planet, alongside tens of thousands of defunct spacecrafts, rocket parts and debris from payloads breaking up.

Studies have warned that metal particles from space activities – such as rocket launches and satellite reentries – could affect atmospheric chemistry and the ozone layer, while the UN has warned increased space activity poses risks to ground safety, darkness and astronomy.

While satellites don't yet overwhelm the sky to the naked eye, Larsen worries about the future state of the night sky. He hopes his image will ignite debate and reflection over how satellites can be used responsibly.

"We can raise awareness, and through that get a groundswell of support for protecting the night sky."

articles.title: Temporal em Campinas e Hortolândia provoca pontos de alagamento | G1
articles.standfirst: Chuva forte foi registrada na tarde deste sábado (7) e deixou ruas alagadas em Campinas e Hortolândia.
articles.summary: Temporal em Campinas e Hortolândia deixou a região do antigo kartódromo do Taquaral e ruas do Jardim São Jorge cobertas de água na tarde deste sábado (7).
articles.body:
O temporal da tarde deste sábado (7) provocou pontos de alagamento e quedas de árvore na região de Campinas (SP).

Na metrópole, a Defesa Civil informou que o maior índice acumulado de chuvas chegou a 38 mm na região do Parque Oziel e a velocidade dos ventos foi de 37 km/h com rajadas que chegaram a 70 km/h.

Já na cidade de Hortolândia (SP), a chuva forte alagou a Rua Espírito Santo, no Jardim São Jorge.

Em Americana (SP), uma árvore caiu e atingiu a área administrativa da Escola Estadual Gabriel de Oliveira. Em nota, a direção informou que acionou a Defesa Civil para avaliar as condições do prédio.

"As providências necessárias serão adotadas após a avaliação técnica do órgão", diz a nota.

Temporal provoca pontos de alagamento na região do Taquaral, em Campinas (SP) — Foto: Reprodução

Ainda seguro a Prefeitura de Campinas, a cidade registrou 22 ocorrências até 17h30, sendo 18 quedas de árvores, dois alagamentos em vias e dois alagamentos em imóveis.

Heitor Penteado, junto ao Kartódromo, com bloqueio do acesso

Rua Cônego Manoel Garcia, no Jardim Chapadão

Avenida Carlos Grimaldi, no Jardim Chapadão

Rua Manoel Antunes Novo, em Barão Geraldo

Rua Valentina Penteado de Freitas, no Parque das Universidades

A prefeitura de Campinas informou que, em razão das fortes chuvas, cancelou a apresentação do espetáculo “TOP 10 da Galinha Pintadinha”, prevista para este sábado (7) às 16h, no Teatro de Arena do Centro de Convivência Cultural Carlos Gomes.

As crianças e famílias que já estavam no espaço foram acolhidas no saguão do Centro de Convivência. No local, tiveram a oportunidade de encontrar a personagem Galinha Pintadinha e registrar fotos.

Não foi possível transferir a apresentação para o teatro interno do Centro de Convivência, pois o espaço já estava reservado para receber o concerto Carmina Burana, da Orquestra Sinfônica de Campinas, cuja programação também ocorre neste sábado.

Chuva forte causa alagamento na Avenida Princesa d'Oeste, em Campinas — Foto: Reprodução

A região está sob alerta de "perigo" para o risco de tempestades severas, de acordo com alerta publicado pelo Instituto Nacional de Meteorologia (Inmet).

Isso significa que as cidades podem registrar chuvas de até 100 milímetros por dia, além de ventos intensos de 60 a 100 km/h e queda de granizo.

Em caso de rajadas de vento, o Inmet orienta:

não se abrigue debaixo de árvores, pois há risco de queda e descargas elétricas;

não estacione veículos próximos a torres de transmissão e placas de propaganda;

se possível, desligue aparelhos elétricos e quadro geral de energia;

A Defesa Civil pode ser acionada por meio do telefone 199. O Corpo de Bombeiros atende pelo 193.

articles.title: Malária no Amazonas: casos caem 29% e são os menores desde 2016 | G1
articles.standfirst: Ao todo, foram registrados 38.149 casos, o menor número para esses meses desde 2016. Os dados foram divulgados na sexta-feira (6), Dia da Malária nas Américas.
articles.summary: A queda nos casos de malária no Amazonas reflete o avanço do tratamento com tafenoquina e novas estratégias de vigilância em saúde adotadas em todo o estado.
articles.body:
Mosquito Anopheles darlingi, principal transmissor da malária na América do Sul. — Foto: Romuald Carinci e Pascal Gaborit/Institut Pasteur de la Guyane

O número de casos de malária no Amazonas caiu 29% entre janeiro e outubro de 2026 , em comparação com o mesmo período do ano passado. Ao todo, foram registrados 38.149 casos, o menor número para esses meses desde 2016, segundo dados preliminares da Fundação de Vigilância em Saúde do Amazonas – Dra. Rosemary Costa Pinto (FVS-RCP).

Os dados foram divulgados na sexta-feira (6), Dia da Malária nas Américas. A data também marcou o encerramento de uma reunião regional sobre a eliminação da doença, promovida pela Organização Pan-Americana da Saúde ( Opas ), em Brasília .

Durante o encontro, a FVS-RCP apresentou estratégias adotadas no Amazonas para combater a malária, incluindo o uso de novas tecnologias e medicamentos.

Uma das estratégias apresentadas foi o uso da tafenoquina, medicamento utilizado no tratamento da malária . Segundo a FVS-RCP, a opção já está disponível em 33 municípios do estado para o tratamento de adultos.

A versão pediátrica do medicamento também começou a ser implementada e já chegou a 27 municípios. Ao todo, 14.813 pessoas foram tratadas com a tafenoquina no Amazonas.

A diretora-presidente da fundação, Tatyana Amorim, atribuiu a redução dos casos ao trabalho de vigilância, à atuação conjunta com os municípios e à adoção de novas tecnologias.

"A redução dos casos de malária é resultado de um trabalho que envolve vigilância epidemiológica, inovação e atuação conjunta com os municípios. A incorporação de novas tecnologias e a qualificação dos profissionais permitem desenvolver estratégias mais adequadas à realidade amazônica, contribuindo para o diagnóstico oportuno, o tratamento e a proteção da população", salientou Tatyana.

Apesar da redução, o Amazonas ainda registra um número expressivo de casos da doença . Por isso, a FVS-RCP reforça a importância da prevenção e do diagnóstico rápido.

O diretor de Vigilância Ambiental da fundação, Elder Figueiredo, orienta que pessoas com sintomas procurem uma unidade de saúde e sigam o tratamento até o fim.

"Ainda temos um número expressivo de casos de malária no Amazonas, o que demonstra a importância de manter as ações preventivas. Ao apresentar sintomas, a população deve procurar imediatamente uma unidade de saúde para realizar o diagnóstico e seguir o tratamento até o fim", orienta o diretor.

articles.title: Ventos de 96 km/h derrubam árvores e afetam energia elétrica na região | G1
articles.standfirst: Em Piracicaba, rajadas provocaram ao menos 19 quedas de árvores; em Santa Bárbara d'Oeste, falta de energia comprometeu sistemas de captação e tratamento de água.
articles.summary: Em Piracicaba, rajadas provocaram ao menos 19 quedas de árvores; em Santa Bárbara d'Oeste, falta de energia comprometeu sistemas de captação e tratamento de água.
articles.body:
O temporal que atingiu Piracicaba e Santa Bárbara d'Oeste na tarde deste sábado (7) provocou uma série de transtornos, com queda de árvores, interrupções no fornecimento de energia elétrica, danos em estruturas públicas e impactos no abastecimento de água.

Em Piracicaba, uma estação do Instituto Nacional de Meteorologia (Inmet) registrou rajadas de vento de até 96,1 km/h às 16h , segundo a Defesa Civil do Estado. O município contabilizou ao menos 19 ocorrências de queda de árvores e galhos em diferentes bairros.

Os registros foram feitos em regiões como Tupi, Nova Piracicaba, Jupiá, Nova América, Jardim São Jorge, Higienópolis, Terras do Engenho, São Dimas, Centro, Jardim Elite e Dois Córregos.

Equipes da prefeitura, da Defesa Civil, do Corpo de Bombeiros e da CPFL foram mobilizadas para a retirada de árvores, desobstrução de vias e atendimento de situações de risco.

Rajadas de até 96 km/h derrubam árvores e danificam estruturas em Piracicaba — Foto: Arquivo pessoal/Gleison Santos/Michele Fernanda

O temporal também danificou parte da cobertura do Terminal de ônibus da Pauliceia, que permaneceu parcialmente interditado.

Além disso, houve interrupções no fornecimento de energia elétrica na UPA Vila Cristina e em bairros como Castelinho, Santa Rosa, Jupiá e Centro. Na comunidade Pereirinha, uma casa sofreu danos estruturais.

Em nota, a CPFL Paulista informou que os problemas foram causados principalmente pela queda de árvores de grande porte e objetos arremessados pelo vento sobre a fiação.

"Em alguns trechos, os danos foram extensos e será necessário reconstruir estruturas que foram destruídas. Todas as equipes foram rapidamente mobilizadas e estão atuando para restabelecer a energia aos clientes afetados, em segurança, no menor tempo possível", informou a empresa.

⚠️ A CPFL Paulista alerta para que ninguém toque em fios partidos ou galhos de árvores que estejam caídos sobre a rede elétrica. "Acione imediatamente a CPFL e a Defesa Civil, e aguarde o atendimento."

Temporal que atingiu Piracicaba (SP) neste sábado (7) danificou parte da cobertura do Terminal de ônibus da Pauliceia — Foto: Edjan Del Santo

Em Santa Bárbara d'Oeste a ventania derrubou árvores em diferentes pontos da cidade. Em um dos casos, uma árvore caiu sobre um carro estacionado . Ninguém se feriu.

No início da noite, o Departamento de Água e Esgoto (DAE) informou que a falta de energia causada pelo temporal atingiu o sistema de captação da Represinha e as Estações de Tratamento de Água (ETAs), interrompendo os sistemas de bombeamento .

Segundo a autarquia, a situação pode comprometer o abastecimento de água em diferentes regiões do município . Equipes do DAE e da CPFL atuavam para restabelecer a energia e normalizar a operação dos sistemas.

Diante do cenário, o órgão orientou os moradores a utilizarem de forma racional a água armazenada em caixas d'água, consumindo apenas o necessário até a regularização dos serviços .

articles.title: 'Agradeço a Deus que estou vivo', diz homem ferido em tornado no RS | G1
articles.standfirst: Fenômeno atingiu Santo Augusto na madrugada deste sábado (7). Tempestades atingiram diferentes regiões do estado. Há registros de alagamentos e famílias fora de casa no interior do estado.
articles.summary: Fenômeno atingiu Santo Augusto na madrugada deste sábado (7). Tempestades atingiram diferentes regiões do estado. Há registros de alagamentos e familias fora de casa no interior do
articles.body:
A passagem de um tornado por Santo Augusto , na Região Noroeste do estado, na madrugada deste sábado (7), deixou um homem ferido . O trabalhador autônomo Maurício Padilha Dias conta que estava dormindo e acordou com o barulho do fenômeno.

"Agradeço a Deus que estou vivo, o importante é que eu estou vivo, e a família também está viva. A gente vai reconstruir aos poucos, devagarinho", diz.

Segundo ele, o vento forte destruiu uma das janelas da casa, que acabou caindo sobre ele . O corte fez com que o homem precisasse ser internado em um hospital da região.

"Quando vi, deu aquele estouro violento, arrebentou a janela e caiu por cima de mim. Foi muito fundo o corte", conta Dias, que levou sete pontos na região da cabeça .

A Defesa Civil do Rio Grande do Sul confirmou neste sábado que o fenômeno que atingiu a cidade foi um tornado . A força do vento destelhou cerca de 100 casas.

Este foi o segundo tornado registrado no estado nesta semana . O primeiro havia atingido as cidades de Erval Grande, Itatiba do Sul e Barra do Rio Azul, no Norte gaúcho , na manhã de quarta-feira (4). Desde a segunda-feira (2), a Região Sul do Brasil teve seis tornados: três em Santa Catarina, um no Paraná e dois no RS.

A madrugada foi marcada por tempestades com vento e granizo, que deixaram danos em cidades de diferentes regiões do estado . Há registro de pelo menos outra pessoa ferida . A segunda vítima foi uma pessoa que teve ferimentos leves após uma árvore cair sobre o veículo que ela dirigia , em Bento Gonçalves , na Serra.

Bento Gonçalves registrou danos em residências causados por grandes pedras de granizo. Nas primeiras horas do dia, moradores formaram filas em frente ao quartel do Corpo de Bombeiros para retirar lonas.

Segundo a Prefeitura de Bento Gonçalves, as ocorrências foram registradas, principalmente, na zona norte do município. Mais de 500 atendimentos foram realizados e, até o início da manhã, mais de 350 moradores buscaram lonas.

Também na Serra, a cidade de Caxias do Sul foi atingida e quatro residências tiveram danos . Em Canela , os moradores registraram granizo perto das 4h. A prefeitura informou que recebeu um chamado em função do vento. Na localidade de Tubiana, no interior do município, houve queda de árvores e o destelhamento de um galpão .

Em São Borja , na Fronteira Oeste, a chuva forte causou alagamentos, destelhamentos e bloqueios de vias. A elevação do Rio Uruguai provocou novas saídas de moradores de áreas atingidas pelas cheias. Famílias que haviam retornado para casa há pouco mais de uma semana precisaram deixar os imóveis novamente.

Os temporais atingiram, ainda, cidades do Norte do Rio Grande do Sul. Em Passo Fundo , choveu 80 milímetros em 24 horas. Durante a madrugada, foram registrados alagamentos. Cerca de 15 kits de lonas foram entregues a moradores e duas pontes na área urbana precisaram ser interditadas.

Só nesta semana, Passo Fundo já registrou mais de 250 milímetros de precipitação. Na quarta-feira, o município já havia contabilizado estragos por conta do tempo severo, com mais de seis mil pessoas atingidas por alagamentos e destelhamentos.

Em Palmeira das Missões , cinco residências foram totalmente destruídas. A Defesa Civil municipal faz o levantamento das demais casas que tiveram danos, principalmente nos telhados.

Em Coxilha , a chuva acompanhada de vento forte causou destruição em propriedades rurais. Segundo a prefeitura, houve danos em telhados de casas e galpões no limite com Passo Fundo. Apesar dos estragos, não há feridos ou desalojados no município.

Já em Getúlio Vargas , o Rio Abaúna ultrapassou a cota de inundação e causou alagamentos no centro da cidade. Durante a madrugada, choveu mais de 96 milímetros. O município também registrou queda de granizo e mais de quatro mil raios. Segundo a Defesa Civil, o nível do rio já começou a baixar.

articles.summary: Pelo menos oito voos foram desviados para Campinas neste sábado (7) por conta do temporal em outras cidades. Entre eles, seis operações que desceriam em Congonhas.
articles.body:
A chegada do temporal à região de Campinas (SP) trouxe a formação de uma "nuvem prateleira" , que cobriu o Aeroporto de Viracopos na tarde deste sábado (7). Durante a chuva, o terminal operou por instrumentos, mas não registrou impactos.

Segundo a concessionária que administra Viracopos, pelo menos oito voos foram desviados para Campinas por conta do temporal em outras cidades . Entre eles, seis operações que desceriam em Congonhas .

Segundo os meteorologistas, a "nuvem prateleira" é um fenômeno provocado pelo deslocamento de uma frente fria e geralmente está associado a nuvens de chuva, segundo os meteorologistas.

☁️ Entenda: a frente fria empurra o ar quente e joga rapidamente para cima, formando camadas em formato de rolo, o que causa a aparência de uma prateleira.

Nuvem prateleira encobre o Aeroporto de Viracopos, em Campinas (SP), na tarde deste sábado (7); terminal operou por instrumentos e recebeu voos desviados de outros terminais — Foto: Arquivo pessoal

O temporal da tarde deste sábado (7) provocou pontos de alagamento e quedas de árvore na região de Campinas (SP) .

Na metrópole, a Defesa Civil informou que acumulado de chuvas chegou a 21mm na região central e a velocidade dos ventos foi de 37 km/h com rajadas que chegaram a 70 km/h.

articles.title: Presidente de Israel escolhe rival de Netanyahu para tentar formar novo governo | G1
articles.standfirst: Isaac Herzog escolheu Gadi Eisenkot após o ex-militar e líder da oposição receber o apoio de 67 parlamentares, com ajuda dos partidos árabes.
articles.summary: Isaac Herzog escolheu Gadi Eisenkot após o ex-militar e líder da oposição receber o apoio de 67 parlamentares, com ajuda dos partidos árabes.
articles.body:
O ex-chefe do Estado-Maior de Israel, Gadi Eisenkot, líder do partido Yashar, agita uma bandeira do país. — Foto: Shir Torem / Reuters

O presidente de Israel , Isaac Herzog, escolheu neste sábado (7) Gadi Eisenkot, principal adversário do primeiro-ministro Benjamin Netanyahu , para tentar formar um novo governo . A decisão ocorre após uma eleição sem resultado decisivo, que deixou os dois políticos sem apoio suficiente para assumir o poder.

Segundo o jornal local "Times of Israel", a cerimônia de oficilização deve acontecer no próximo domingo (8), às 17h no horário local (12h no horário de Brasília). Eisenkot terá, então, 28 dias para formar um governo. Se necessário, Herzog poderá conceder a ele uma prorrogação de até 14 dias.

"Este é o momento de formar um governo de emergência nacional. Farei tudo o que estiver ao meu alcance para garantir que estejamos à altura da responsabilidade", escreveu Eisenkot no X, momentos após o anúncio de sua vitória.

O ex-militar e líder da oposição a Netanyahu recebeu o endosso dos principais partidos árabes-israelenses na última sexta-feira (6). Com seus números somados, a sigla de oposição obteve suporte de 67 deputados no Knesset, o parlamento isaraelense.

São necessárias 61 das 120 cadeiras para formar governo.

A eleição realizada em 27 de outubro terminou sem que nenhum dos dois principais blocos conquistasse a maioria necessária para governar . O partido Likud, de Netanyahu, foi o mais votado e conquistou 27 cadeiras. Mas a aliança de partidos de direita e religiosos ligada ao premiê ficou com 53 vagas do parlamento.

O bloco de oposição ligado a Eisenkot, líder do partido Yashar, obteve 48.

O resultado também marcou o avanço dos partidos que representam a população árabe de Israel. As duas principais forças do grupo conquistaram juntas 19 cadeiras, um recorde.

O crescimento ocorreu em meio a uma participação recorde de eleitores árabes , que representam cerca de 21% da população do país.

As duas legendas anunciaram apoio a Eisenkot durante as consultas com o presidente Isaac Herzog. Com isso, o ex-chefe do Estado-Maior passou a contar com o endosso de 67 parlamentares, acima do mínimo necessário para governar.

O apoio, porém, não significa que os partidos árabes farão parte de uma eventual coalizão. Eisenkot já afirmou que não pretende incluí-los no governo.

Filho de imigrantes marroquinos, Eisenkot, de 66 anos, poderá ser o primeiro premiê de Israel integrante da comunidade mizrahi, formada por judeus cujas famílias têm origem no Oriente Médio e no norte da África.

Discreto e avesso à exposição na imprensa, Eisenkot entrou na política apenas em 2022. Ele integrou brevemente o gabinete de guerra de Netanyahu após o ataque do Hamas a Israel, em 7 de outubro de 2023 , mas depois voltou à oposição.

Como opositor, criticou publicamente a liderança de Netanyahu, incluindo a condução da ofensiva militar na Faixa de Gaza. Eisenkot também prometeu que não participaria de um governo liderado pelo atual primeiro-ministro.

A trajetória política de Eisenkot também é marcada pelas perdas pessoais de sua família desde 2023. Um filho e dois sobrinhos dele morreram em combate na Faixa de Gaza.

Durante a campanha eleitoral, Eisenkot destacou sua experiência na área de segurança. Ele citou a chamada "Doutrina Dahiya", estratégia que prevê respostas militares desproporcionais a ataques. O ex-general empregou essa abordagem quando comandou operações durante a guerra de 2006 entre Israel e o Hezbollah, grupo apoiado pelo Irã que atua no Líbano.

Eisenkot também criticou a violência de colonos israelenses contra palestinos, que aumentou desde 2023 e elevou as tensões nas relações de Israel com países ocidentais.

Ele se opõe ainda aos aliados de extrema direita de Netanyahu, Itamar Ben-Gvir e Bezalel Smotrich. Os dois já foram alvo de sanções de alguns países ocidentais por declarações consideradas incitação à violência contra palestinos.

articles.title: Agentes penitenciários condenados por tortura em Salvador | G1
articles.standfirst: Violência aconteceu durante uma revista nas celas, em junho de 2010. Presos relataram socos, chutes, golpes de cassetetes e choques elétricos. Condenados receberam penas de até 13 anos e sete meses de prisão.
articles.summary: Agentes penitenciários condenados por tortura em Salvador perderam cargos e devem indenizar 260 detentos agredidos com choques e cassetetes em uma revista de 2010.
articles.body:
Justiça condena 31 agentes penitenciários e diretores por tortura contra 260 presos em cadeia pública de Salvador — Foto: Seap

Trinta e um agentes penitenciários, coordenadores e integrantes da direção da Cadeia Pública de Salvador foram condenados por tortura contra 260 presos durante uma revista realizada na unidade, em 23 de junho de 2010. As penas chegam a 13 anos, sete meses e dez dias de prisão, em regime inicial fechado.

A sentença foi assinada em 24 de outubro de 2026 pelo juiz Bernardo Mario Dantas Lubambo, da 14ª Vara Criminal de Salvador. O caso começou a repercutir neste sábado (7).

Segundo a decisão, os internos foram submetidos a agressões físicas e verbais durante a ação. Entre as violências relatadas estão socos, chutes, pontapés, tapas, golpes de cassetetes, humilhações e choques elétricos.

Na época, 412 pessoas estavam custodiadas na unidade. Desse total, 260 teriam sido vítimas das agressões.

A revista foi apresentada inicialmente como um procedimento de rotina para evitar possíveis motins. No entanto, conforme a sentença, a ação também teria sido utilizada como forma de castigo aos presos por reivindicações anteriores e para intimidá-los a não promover novas rebeliões.

Em nota, a Secretaria de Administração Penitenciária e Ressocialização (Seap) informou que os fatos citados na decisão judicial ocorreram em 2010, antes da atual gestão. A pasta afirmou respeitar a decisão da Justiça e disse não compactuar com práticas de violência ilegal ou violações dos direitos humanos.

Também destacou que tem investido na capacitação dos policiais penais, com foco no respeito aos direitos das pessoas privadas de liberdade, e reafirmou a confiança no trabalho dos profissionais que atuam nas unidades prisionais. (Veja a íntegra do posicionamento no final da reportagem)

O g1 também tenta contato com as defesas dos condenados.

O episódio chegou ao conhecimento das autoridades depois que familiares dos presos identificaram marcas de agressões nos corpos dos internos e procuraram o Ministério Público.

Uma inspeção judicial realizada na Cadeia Pública constatou hematomas e ferimentos em diversos detentos. Durante a apuração, também foram reunidos depoimentos de presos e agentes penitenciários, reconhecimentos de suspeitos, registros médicos e fotografias das lesões.

Na sentença, o magistrado reconheceu a participação de agentes penitenciários nas agressões. Também apontou a responsabilidade de integrantes da direção da unidade, que teriam presenciado os acontecimentos e deixado de impedir a continuidade da violência.

Justiça condena 31 agentes penitenciários e diretores por tortura contra 260 presos em cadeia pública de Salvador — Foto: Arquivo Pessoal

As penas foram definidas de acordo com a função exercida por cada um e a participação reconhecida na sentença.

Agentes penitenciários — 11 anos e 8 meses de prisão:

Todos receberam penas em regime inicial fechado.

Coordenadores — 13 anos, 7 meses e 10 dias de prisão:

Gilberto José Santos, coordenador de segurança;

Jessé Alves Gomes, coordenador de vigilância;

Luiz Carlos Souza Sacramento, coordenador de vigilância.

Diretores da Cadeia Pública — 13 anos, 7 meses e 10 dias de prisão:

Clésio Rômulo Atanásio Sobrinho, diretor-adjunto;

Everaldo Jesus de Carvalho, diretor-geral.

Condenados também perderam cargos públicos

Além das penas de prisão, os 31 condenados perderam os cargos, funções ou empregos públicos que ocupavam. A sentença também determinou que eles fiquem proibidos de exercer as respectivas funções pelo dobro do tempo das penas aplicadas.

O juiz estabeleceu ainda uma indenização mínima de R$ 5 mil para cada vítima relacionada na denúncia. O valor deverá ser pago proporcionalmente pelos condenados, com juros de 1% ao mês e correção monetária pelo Índice Nacional de Preços ao Consumidor (INPC), desde a data dos fatos.

A sentença também determinou a absolvição de três pessoas: Edna de Aquino Brito, Cláudio José Silva Cavalcanti e Alexssandro Andrade Mainart.

Já em relação a Paulo Sérgio de Sousa Silva, a Justiça reconheceu a extinção da punibilidade em razão da morte dele.

"A Secretaria de Administração Penitenciária e Ressocialização (SEAP) esclarece que os fatos mencionados na decisão judicial ocorreram em 2010, há mais de 16 anos, muito antes da atual gestão.

A Secretaria respeita a decisão da Justiça e reafirma que não compactua com qualquer prática de violência ilegal ou violação dos direitos humanos.

Na atual gestão, temos intensificado a capacitação e a qualificação dos policiais penais, com foco no respeito aos direitos humanos e na preservação da integridade física das pessoas privadas de liberdade.

Confiamos plenamente no trabalho sério e comprometido dos nossos policiais penais, que diariamente garantem a segurança, a disciplina e o desenvolvimento das ações de ressocialização nas unidades prisionais.

Seguimos firmes na valorização desses profissionais, no respeito à legalidade e no compromisso de transformar o sistema prisional da Bahia em um sistema cada vez mais eficiente, justo e, sobretudo, humanizado."

articles.title: Fórmula 1 renova contrato com São Paulo e garante GP de Interlagos até 2035 | G1
articles.standfirst: Acordo amplia em cinco anos o vínculo da categoria com a capital paulista; corrida recebeu 303 mil torcedores em 2025.
articles.summary: Acordo amplia em cinco anos o vínculo da categoria com a capital paulista; corrida recebeu 303 mil torcedores em 2025.
articles.body:
Vista aérea do autódromo de Interlagos, na Zona Sul de SP, onde é realizado o GP Brasil de Fórmula 1 — Foto: Luis Moura/Estadão Conteúdo

Segundo comunicado divulgado pela Fórmula 1, a renovação prevê a continuidade dos investimentos da Prefeitura de São Paulo na estrutura do autódromo para garantir a realização do evento.

O presidente e CEO da categoria, Stefano Domenicali, afirmou ao ge que o Brasil tem papel importante na história da Fórmula 1 e destacou a participação dos torcedores brasileiros.

"O Brasil é uma parte importante na história da Fórmula 1 e do nosso futuro, e eu estou muito feliz por essa extensão de cinco anos nos permitir continuar correndo em São Paulo até 2035. A paixão de nossos fãs brasileiros é extraordinária, e toda vez que nós retornamos a Interlagos sentimos a energia deles nas arquibancadas e na cidade de São Paulo", disse.

O prefeito Ricardo Nunes (MDB) também comemorou a renovação. Segundo ele, a extensão do contrato permite planejar novos investimentos e manter a cidade no circuito de grandes eventos internacionais.

"São Paulo tem uma longa tradição e uma relação histórica com a Fórmula 1. Manter essa parceria significa garantir a previsibilidade para investimentos, fortalecer o calendário de grandes eventos e consolidar a posição da cidade como uma referência global para sediar competições internacionais", afirmou.

CEO do Grande Prêmio de São Paulo, Alan Adler disse, em entrevista ao ge , que a renovação representa motivo de orgulho e agradeceu à categoria e à prefeitura pelos investimentos feitos na modernização de Interlagos.

O executivo também destacou a importância histórica do circuito, que recebe provas da Fórmula 1 há décadas e é reconhecido por pilotos, equipes e torcedores de diferentes países.

Ao longo da história do Grande Prêmio do Brasil, cinco pilotos brasileiros venceram a prova. Ayrton Senna, Emerson Fittipaldi, Felipe Massa e José Carlos Pace conquistaram vitórias em Interlagos. Nelson Piquet venceu no antigo circuito de Jacarepaguá, no Rio de Janeiro.

Neste domingo (8), o país também terá a estreia de seu 34º piloto na Fórmula 1: o pernambucano Rafael Câmara, da Haas. O último brasileiro a chegar à categoria havia sido Gabriel Bortoleto, atualmente na Audi.

Público e crescimento da categoria no país

Dados divulgados pela Fórmula 1 apontam que a categoria tem aproximadamente 5,5 milhões de seguidores nas redes sociais no Brasil. Entre os fãs brasileiros, 44% são mulheres e 41% têm menos de 35 anos.

Em 2025, o Grande Prêmio de São Paulo recebeu 303 mil pessoas ao longo do fim de semana de atividades no autódromo. O número superou o registrado em 2024, quando 291 mil torcedores acompanharam a programação em Interlagos.

Operação mobiliza mil policiais por dia para reforçar segurança do GP de Fórmula 1 em SP — Foto: Divulgação/SSP

articles.title: In 2016, Jim Carrey bought a Maui oceanfront retreat for $16.5 million; after listing it for $35 million in October 2026, he found a buyer within weeks, though the final sale price is not yet known
articles.summary: For nearly a decade, Jim Carrey’s Hawaiian retreat provided him with something Hollywood rarely could — privacy, solitude and the calming presence of the
articles.body: For nearly a decade, Jim Carrey’s Hawaiian retreat provided him with something Hollywood rarely could — privacy, solitude and the calming presence of the Pacific Ocean. The property is located on just under an acre of prime beachfront land on Maui and is designed to blur the lines between indoor living and the tropical landscape outside. Now the actor looks ready to let go of the stunning estate. Carrey has already sold the property he listed in October 2026 for $35 million, another significant real estate move for the Hollywood star as he enters a new chapter of his personal life.Terminates 10 years of ownershipAs per Realtor report, Carrey purchased the oceanfront property in 2016 for $16.5 million, said the realtor. His current asking price is $35 million, more than double what he originally paid for it. The Realtor’s property records show that the home is in pending status, which means a buyer is in place, but the amount of the sale has not been released.The property sits on nearly an acre of beachfront land at Keawakapu Beach where South Kihei Road meets the Wailea resort area. The property has approximately 170 feet of ocean frontage, with a wide green lawn and tall coconut palms between the houses and the shore.The estate was designed by architecture firm Ike Kligerman Barkley, with the goal of weaving traditional Hawaiian influences into a sprawling contemporary retreat, states a report by James Edition. Architectural details include thatched roofing, Douglas fir framing, and woven bamboo finishes.Two houses with a view of the PacificThe property is 4,717 square feet and was built in 2002, and is spread out over two separate buildings. The main residence has the primary living areas and a main bedroom suite, while a second building provides independent accommodation for guests.The main house has three bedrooms in total across the accommodation of the estate and the guest structure has two further bedrooms with their own bathrooms. The property also has four and a half bathrooms.One of the characteristics is the great room with high ceilings and wooden trusses that create the airy atmosphere. Big openings connect the interiors to a covered stone lanai, allowing residents to flow easily between the inside and outside.The chef's kitchen has two oversized islands, white cabinetry and premium appliances, according to Realtor. The master suite has another unique feature: a swinging bed and floor-to-ceiling windows, and its bathroom features a statement soaking tub and dual vanities.A resort at homeThe outdoor spaces are the estate’s biggest attractions. A freeform swimming pool snakes through natural rock formations in between the two buildings. The design features a hidden grotto, a water slide, a shallow lounging ledge and an elevated spa.According to The James Edition, one of the property’s most valuable features is its generous beachfront setting. Its placement allows both buildings to have ocean views and still have a good stretch of landscaped grounds between the residences and the sand.The listing is with Hawaii Life’s Blake Hill and the estate is being sold fully furnished and in excellent condition. "It is an unusual offering in the luxury property market of Maui with its combination of architectural design, privacy and direct beach access."A more quiet life away from HollywoodCarrey's relationship with Maui reflects a broader shift in his lifestyle over the past decade. The actor gradually slipped from the limelight into a more private existence after becoming one of Hollywood's most recognizable comedy stars in 1994 with films such as Ace Ventura: Pet Detective, The Mask and Dumb and Dumber.James Edition notes that his island routine has mostly involved reading, writing, walking, painting and sketching. Carrey has also expressed his desire to retire from acting and lead a quieter life away from the demands of the entertainment industry.His private life, too, has entered a new phase. The actor recently wed his longtime love, Min Ah, in an intimate Los Angeles ceremony, Realtor reports. The couple have kept their relationship largely private, making the development a major milestone.Another major real estate exitCarrey’s listing in Maui comes after he sold his longtime estate in Brentwood, Los Angeles. The two-acre property was purchased in 1994 for $3.8 million and was first listed in February 2023 for $28.9 million.According to Realtor, however, it was difficult to find a buyer. After several price cuts, the home finally sold in 2024 for $17 million,Carrey now has a buyer for his Hawaiian retreat and appears to be letting go of another major property. It’s not clear whether he plans to have a home elsewhere in Hawaii or to establish his business in California. Its new owner has a new chapter ahead for the Maui estate, though the final sale price has not been disclosed.Images Courtesy: Instagram/jimcarrey and RealtorReady to Make a Smarter Property Decision? articles.title: 'Keeping Sanjay in check could have prevented damage': Sonia Gandhi on Emergency
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Congress Parliamentary Party chairperson Sonia Gandhi has described the imposition of the Emergency as a mistake, saying she believes her
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Congress Parliamentary Party chairperson Sonia Gandhi has described the imposition of the Emergency as a mistake, saying she believes her mother-in-law and then prime minister Indira Gandhi eventually came to regret the decision.The Congress leader in her upcoming book "Belonging: A Journey of Love" also writes that keeping Sanjay Gandhi "in check" could have prevented much of the damage that followed the imposition of the Emergency, according to her interview with The Guardian ahead of the book’s release."I always feel that Mrs (Indira) Gandhi was a democrat at heart," Sonia told the British daily. "I know that many would laugh at this, but I believe she was never comfortable in the course of the emergency. I think it was sitting heavy on her," she added.How the Emergency divided the Gandhi familyAccording to The Guardian, Sonia recalled that the decision to impose the Emergency divided the family.Her husband, Rajiv Gandhi, had reportedly advised his mother to wait until the next election, while Sanjay argued that the opposition would destroy her and had to be stopped.Sonia said the disagreement also created tensions within the family, as Rajiv tried to confront his mother but she refused to listen."Keeping Sanjay in check could have prevented much of the damage that followed," she wrote in the book, according to The Guardian.In a separate interview with The Hindu, published on Saturday, Sonia said Sanjay was not the only person who influenced the decision.She pointed to pressure from some of Indira's senior colleagues and said few people around the then prime minister shared Rajiv's views."It was not only Sanjay, though in the public mind he is often seen as synonymous with the Emergency. There was a lot of pressure from some of her senior colleagues, and I think there were very few people around her like Rajiv who had a different point of view," she said."I think eventually my mother-in-law began to understand the situation through her own wisdom and took actions to remedy it," she added.Indira later acknowledged Emergency excessesSonia said she became aware of the full gravity of the events only after the Emergency ended. While acknowledging that democratic rights had been curtailed and habeas corpus suspended, she said the measures had been taken constitutionally."It was only after the Emergency that I came to know the true gravity of what had been happening. Yes, democratic rights had been curtailed and there was a suspension of habeas corpus, but it was done constitutionally," she said.Looking back, Sonia said Indira had been struggling to deal with the deteriorating situation at the time."Yet, when I take myself back to that period and try and see it from Mrs Indira Gandhi's point of view, I see her struggling to cope with the rapidly deteriorating prevailing circumstances: violent protests, government offices and public transport set on fire, widespread organised unrest and even a call for the bureaucracy and armed forces to disobey orders," she said.Sonia said hindsight helped put the events into perspective. She also pointed out that Indira later called elections and publicly expressed regret over the excesses committed during the Emergency."And you know very well that she herself later publicly expressed regret and apologised for excesses during the Emergency," she said.Sonia recalls Babri mosque demolitionIn her interview with The Guardian, Sonia also recalled crying as she watched the Babri mosque being demolished in December 1992.She said the incident made her realise that the country faced "a long battle for the secular nation that Mahatma Gandhi, Nehru and their colleagues had strived to build", the British daily reported.Sonia also acknowledged that the Congress had, in part, contributed to the rise of the BJP and its hardline Hindutva politics."I think we have been too complacent in many ways. There was a laissez-faire kind of an attitude," she said.Indira Gandhi imposed the Emergency shortly before midnight on June 25, 1975. President Fakhruddin Ali Ahmed issued the proclamation on her recommendation, and the Union Cabinet later ratified it.On January 18, 1977, Indira announced fresh Lok Sabha elections and released political prisoners. She and Sanjay Gandhi were defeated in the March 1977 elections. The Emergency officially ended on March 21, 1977.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: At least 6 killed, 15 wounded in Poland shooting; gunman shot
articles.summary: At least six people were killed and 15 wounded after a gunman opened fire in a busy market square in Krakow, Poland's second-largest city, on Saturday,
articles.body: At least six people were killed and 15 wounded after a gunman opened fire in a busy market square in Krakow, Poland's second-largest city, on Saturday, authorities said.The perpetrator targeted random people while driving into the Main Square, a major tourist destination in Krakow's city centre. Police officers were also among the wounded.The shooter is a Polish national, according to police, as reported by local news outlet Onet."The man had no identification documents with him. The police were able to establish his identity through operational work,” the website quoted a police officer as saying.Gunman shot during exchange of fire with policeThe gunman was shot and wounded during an exchange of fire with officers a short distance from the site of the initial shooting.Katarzyna Cisło, a Krakow Police spokesperson, told local broadcaster TVN24 that the perpetrator was wearing military-style fatigues and carrying a military-type long gun.Cisło added that the man acted alone and that the public was safe. articles.title: Third person arrested after car damaged by gunshots in Swansea
articles.summary: A 29-year-old man was taken into custody on Saturday morning following two earlier arrests on Friday.
articles.body:
A third person has been arrested after armed police responded to an incident in which a car was hit by gunshots.

South Wales Police said a vehicle on the A48 in Morriston, Swansea, sustained damage "consistent with a firearms discharge" on Friday and one person was left with minor injuries.

A 41-year-old man, from Llansamlet, and a 16-year-old boy , also from Llansamlet, were arrested in the aftermath on Friday and remain in custody.

On Saturday police said a 29-year-old man from Swansea had also now been arrested on suspicion of affray and possessing an offensive weapon.

Police continue to investigate and are appealing for witnesses and anyone with footage of the incident to come forward.

Ch Supt Stephen Jones, of South Wales Police, said the force believed that the "individuals involved are likely to be known to one another."

"Incidents such as this are rare but we appreciate they cause significant concern within local communities," he said.

The force said it was not currently aware of any wider threat to the public.

Jones said: "A visible policing presence will remain in the area as officers continue their enquiries and provide reassurance to local residents.

"I would like to urge anyone who does have information to make contact."

South Wales Police said it was also aware of rumours and speculation circulating on social media in relation to this incident, and asks the public not to share unverified information.

Residents were told to avoid the area and events, including a local firework display due to take place on Friday, were cancelled.

Video circulating online shows police officers next to a stationary car that appeared to have been struck by a shotgun blast on Clase Road near an Asda superstore.

A National Police Air Service helicopter was circling the area but has since returned to base.

South Wales Police said all road closures put in place following the incident had been lifted.

Anyone who witnessed the incident or who has information or footage that could assist the investigation, is asked to contact South Wales Police via its major incident public portal.

articles.title: A North Carolina student went inside a convenience store after a gas pump failed to print his receipt; the $3 Powerball ticket he bought there won him $2 million
articles.summary: Life does not always go the way we plan. Sometimes, an unexpected detour can lead to something extraordinary.
articles.body: Life does not always go the way we plan. Sometimes, an unexpected detour can lead to something extraordinary. Bram Dunehew, a college student in North Carolina, had no plans of winning $2 million in the lottery when he stopped to refuel his car. The gas pump failed to print his receipt, sending him inside a convenience store. On a spur-of-the-moment decision, he bought a $3 Powerball ticket, which turned into a life-changing Halloween windfall! “It’s crazy because I never would have even bought that ticket if the receipt had printed outside,” Dunehew told the NC Education Lottery.A receipt that changed the course of his lifeOn Friday, October 30, Bram Dunehew stopped for petrol in Harrisburg. The errand should have taken five minutes. Fill the tank, grab the receipt and drive home. But the pump had other plans. After filling the tank, the receipt didn’t print. So Dunehew, a Concord resident studying civil engineering at college, walked inside Sam’s Mart on N.C. 49 to sort it out.While inside the convenience store, he picked up a $3 Powerball ticket. It was a random decision. Nothing about that purchase was planned or special. Never in his wildest dreams did Dunehew think he would win the lottery that weekend. The printer outside was the only reason he went in at all.Five white balls and a Power PlayThe ticket was for Saturday night’s drawing, which fell on Halloween. When the numbers were read, Dunehew had matched all five white balls! He was ecstatic. That alone was worth $1 million. His Power Play option doubled the prize to $2 million!The college student would not have bought the lottery ticket if the gas station’s printer had not malfunctioned. “I think Halloween’s now my favourite holiday. Trick or treating was fun as a kid, but this is insane,” he told the outlet.The odds of winning the Powerball jackpot are 1 in 292 million. Dunehew didn’t hit the jackpot, but the odds still illustrate how rare his prize was. The winners have 180 days from the drawing date to claim their prizes, at the lottery headquarters in Raleigh. After federal and state tax withholdings, he will take home $1,440,201. He plans to use some of the money to buy his father a Cadillac. It is a gift that connects the win to his family, rather than the prize itself.Lottery money has its own story in Cabarrus County, where education programmes received $16 million in lottery support last year. Dunehew’s ticket was a small part of that system, bought on a whim at a counter he only visited because a machine failed.Sometimes these detours take us to places we would otherwise never go. In Dunehew’s case, that detour has brought him a fortune.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: 'We don't take George Michael seriously enough'
articles.summary: Sathnam Sanghera, from Wolverhampton, says the Faith singer is one of the all-time pop music greats.
articles.body:
George Michael is not taken seriously as a cultural figure despite being one of the biggest artists in pop history, an author and self-confessed super fan has said.

Sathnam Sanghera, who wrote Tonight the Music Seems So Loud: The Meaning of George Michael, paid tribute to his hero on the day of the release of The Faith Tour concert film.

The movie hit cinemas on Friday and features performances from the Careless Whisper singer during his 1988 tour to promote the number one album, Faith.

Sanghera, from Wolverhampton, said the film evoked a "powerful" era of live music with Michael's talent on full display.

"It was one of the biggest tours of the 80s and it was hugely significant that it was a British pop star doing this," he told BBC Radio 4's World at One.

"In the late 80s, George Michael was up there with Madonna, Prince and Whitney Houston. This was a white guy from Finchley and Faith was the biggest selling single in America in 1988."

Sanghera said Michael performed for about two million people during the tour and the impact was one of the reasons he chose to write his book.

"We don't take George Michael seriously as a cultural figure," he added, "but he was one of the biggest artists in the history of pop music."

The writer said people would often "take the mickey" out of him for being a fan when Michael was alive, but the teasing declined following the singer's death in 2016.

"No Friday night disco is complete without Wake Me Up Before You Go-Go," he continued. "No wedding disco is complete without Careless Whisper.

"Last Christmas is Christmas. There's so much of his music that's become part of culture. This was not something he was given credit for in his lifetime, it's come afterwards."

He described Michael's voice as "extraordinary" and said he could sing for two hours without hitting a wrong note.

From watching the film, which includes footage from 1988 shows at the Palais Omnisports de Paris-Bercy in Paris, Sanghera said there was a sense of Michael grappling with his sexuality.

He added: "He was increasingly becoming this straight sex symbol, there was all the heterosexual posturing in the videos and also on stage, but inside he knew he was gay."

This was something that came across in many of his songs, said Sanghera, adding that they were often "about a man trying to connect".

"He was a very torn-up, sad man in many ways," he added. "What that gave us is beautiful art. He suffered but, in a really poignant way, we benefited."

articles.body: The US Department of Justice on Friday moved to withdraw its lawsuit seeking to prevent California from counting around 20,000 ballots that it claimed may have been cast by non-citizens, pending verification of their immigration status.The lawsuit, filed in mid-October, was part of President Donald Trump's administration's wider push to increase federal oversight of state-run elections. Trump has repeatedly claimed, without providing evidence, that non-citizens are voting in large numbers. Available data, however, suggests that such instances are extremely rare.The decision came days after Republicans suffered significant setbacks in the midterm elections and roughly a week before a scheduled hearing to examine the reliability of the list of alleged non-citizen voters. A special master was due to assess the accuracy of the list, which California officials have described as outdated and containing eligible voters. The federal judge hearing the case had also criticised the list while rejecting the department's request, according to the Associated Press.The department's motion to dismiss the case said that California would have already irreversibly “commingled the challenged ballots with lawful ones” by the time the hearing takes place. The lawsuit was initiated after ballots had been dispatched to all 23 million registered voters in the state, with hundreds of thousands already processed. Once counted for processing, ballots are fully anonymised.California election officials said the state had processed around 9 million ballots by early Friday, while nearly 5 million were still awaiting counting.Despite seeking to end the case, the Justice Department said on Friday evening that it would continue pursuing suspected violations of election law through other legal proceedings. It is also facing lawsuits from several immigrant and voting rights organisations seeking to restrict its use of the list of suspected non-citizens.Separately, the department filed a motion backing another lawsuit, brought in May, which accuses California of failing to remove ineligible voters from its electoral rolls in accordance with federal voting laws.The move forms part of the administration's continuing efforts to “pursue every available civil and criminal remedy to ensure that only eligible American citizens vote in American elections,” top Los Angeles prosecutor Bill Essayli said, as per AP.You use AI every day. articles.title: Krakow shooting: What we know about gun attack in Poland
articles.summary: Six people were killed in a random shooting in the city's main square, and three bodies were later found at his home.
articles.body:
At least six people were killed and several others injured when a gunman suspected to have ties to the far-right opened fire in central Krakow, the second largest city in Poland.

Three bodies were found at his home when it was searched by police. Here's everything we know so far.

The attack began shortly before 15:00 local time (14:00 GMT) in Krakow's Main Market Square, the bustling central point of the city.

Police said a man drove into the square before beginning to fire "at random people from his car".

Footage from the scene shows scenes of panic as people fled, with the sound of gunfire clearly heard.

A passing tram was shot at during the apparently random attack, shattering windows but no passengers were injured.

Armed officers raced to the scene and engaged in a gunfight with the attacker, who was shot within three minutes of the attack beginning, preventing a further massacre, officials said.

The gunman was shot but is alive and has been arrested.

Distressing footage authenticated by BBC Verify shows the moment a police officer confronts the suspect on the ground before firing his weapon several times.

The officer then falls to the ground, apparently having been injured himself.

Shop windows in the square have signs of damage, seemingly from bullets, with glass shards scattered along the floor.

City officials have urged people who live in the city and tourists to stay away from the area while an investigation continues.

The suspect's car, found at the intersection of Dietla and Stradomska streets, is being checked for possible explosive devices, police say. Residents of nearby buildings are being evacuated while the operation is under way.

How many people have died and been injured?

Six people - four women and two men - are confirmed to have been killed, including a British national. Three victims are Polish and two have not been identified.

Sixteen people, including five foreigners and the attacker, were taken to hospital. Among those being treated are two police officers who were shot while detaining the attacker.

Poland's Prime Minister Donald Tusk later said three bodies - two women and one man - were found at the gunman's house when it was searched after the attack.

One of the police officers was described as being in a "very critical condition" by a Polish government minister after being shot three times while arresting the attacker. The officer is undergoing surgery, he added.

Polish authorities have not confirmed the names and ages of the other victims.

What do we know about the suspect and motive?

Police have identified the attacker as a 25-year-old Polish man but have not confirmed his name.

The suspect was wearing "military-style attire" and had a military-grade weapon, according to a police spokesperson. However, authorities have confirmed the attacker was not a soldier.

"Many pieces of weapons and ammunition were found in his vehicle", the spokesperson added.

Polish media has reported the suspect had a firearms permit and may have obtained the weapons from his family home.

A minister has said early investigations indicate he was inspired by "far-right ideologies". The minister also described him as an "ultra-nationalist" without giving further details.

His home is being searched with support from counter-terrorism police.

The shooting happened in one of the largest medieval squares in Europe, a busy location which is also a popular tourist destination.

Jonathan Balshaw from Ipswich was there with his Polish girlfriend Dominika. The couple were outside St Mary's Basilica, in the corner of the square, when the shooting started.

Jonathan said: "We ran down the side of the church and through the side door and hid with several other people until the gunfire died down.

"A lot of shots were fired, more than 20 with it sounding like multiple different firearms - there were two distinctly different noises."

Caitlin Shasby from Newcastle arrived in Krakow yesterday with her friend Jon for a long weekend.

She said they heard shots from their hotel room but were not sure what was happening until their hotel rang them and told them to "stay in our rooms until further notice".

What has the reaction been in Poland and internationally?

Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk is on his way to Krakow and is expected to give an address later on Saturday.

Earlier, he said he was being kept informed by the interior minister and that police were investigating "the background and all the circumstances".

Krakow Mayor Łukasz Gibała has signed an order declaring a period of mourning in the city which will last until Wednesday, November 11.

President Karol Nawrocki said he was "deeply concerned" and was awaiting "a full explanation of the circumstances surrounding these tragic events".

US ambassador to Poland Tom Rose described it as a "savage and murderous attack".

The EU's top diplomat, Kaja Kallas, said the shooting was "a tragedy that will be felt far beyond Poland".

articles.title: She became Uganda's first wildlife veterinarian and dedicated her career to saving mountain gorillas; Dr. Gladys Kalema-Zikusoka built a model that protects wildlife while supporting local communities
articles.summary: Conservation of nature has become the responsibility of humans. While some are more enthusiastic about it, like Dr.
articles.body: Conservation of nature has become the responsibility of humans. While some are more enthusiastic about it, like Dr. Gladys Kalema-Zikusoka; others are more passive about it. But Dr. Gladys’s story becomes an inspiration about how sometimes nature can pull you back to your roots. She studied abroad, experienced the comforts of life and interacted with people from around the world. Yet, when she returned home, mountain gorillas captured her heart and she ended up dedicating her life to save as many of them. Her story is also motivating to study how local communities should be involved in the process rather than isolated from it.Dr. Kalema-Zikusoka’s interest in saving wildlife wasn’t something she thought of just for the gorillas, her empathy for animals existed since childhood. Kalema told Unearth Women in an interview about a wildlife camp that she set up in her Kampala high school some 30 years ago. This adventure later turned into her career with her attending the University of London’s Royal Veterinary College in the early 1990s. On returning to Uganda at age 25, she was hired as the first female veterinary officer for the country’s national parks.During her time in London, the Uganda wildlife service was exploring the potential of tourism that its large primates including mountain gorillas and chimpanzees could provide. Notably, Uganda, Rwanda, and the Democratic Republic of the Congo are the only three countries with wild mountain gorilla populations. An even more interesting fact is that none of them live in captivity. According to the World Wide Fund, only around 1,063 mountain gorillas are left in the world.The promotion of tourism increased the existing human-animal conflict in the region of Bwindi. While gorillas came out of the forest to feed on human-managed banana plantations, destroying livelihoods of local farmers. Farmers also went into the forest to hunt and gather fuelwood, disturbing the habitat of gorillas.It was in 1994, when she visited Bwindi to conduct summer research on these gorillas. While she initially planned on treating adorable domestic pets, this camp actually changed her life’s road. She felt an instant connection with these primate creatures who were only 600 of them left in Africa then. Around half of them were in Bwindi itself. She observed the threats that these gorillas faced, including hunting, poaching and habitat pressures. There were increasing risks associated with closer contact with humans with the possibility of catching diseases like flu.Around 1996, Kalema-Zikusoka identified that the gorilla community is getting a fatal risk from human scabies. She observed a troop of gorillas whose skin was turning white and scaly which was also making them scratch compulsively. The disease most likely traveled from clothes full of bacteria on the scarecrows. This made her realise the importance of maintaining human health in order to protect the gorillas, so she started promoting hygienic practices to locals.This was the beginning of her community engagement for the purpose of conservation of the mountain gorillas. Later, in 2003, Kalema-Zikusoka founded Conservation Through Public Health (CTPH), a nonprofit based on Bwindi’s border. The organization aimed to promote the health of both gorillas and people alike. For the gorillas, their health was being monitored and thus, treated when required. This included retrieving scat, examining it for pathogens, and darting sick primates with medicine. Human health was equally being focused upon with installing handwashing stations, deworming livestock, and dissuading locals from eating wild game, for the sake of both conservation and disease prevention.This approach taken by her is different from most conservation approaches that focus primarily on protected areas, wildlife patrols or anti-poaching measures. It is based on the approach of One health which implies the interconnectedness of the health of people, animals and the environment. This approach emphasises that local residents are partners in conservation, rather than people expected to protect wildlife without support for their own needs.Turning a cup of coffee into a conservation toolIn 2015, Dr. Gladys Kalema-Zikusoka helped establish another venture. It was the Gorilla Conservation Coffee, a social enterprise designed to give farmers living near Bwindi's mountain gorilla habitat a financial reason to protect the forest. The initiative was clear in its aim with focus on saving livelihoods of local farmers who needed incentives to become part of the conservation story. The initiative works with local coffee growers, paying them a premium for their beans and helping them improve the quality and sustainability of their produce.This gives farmers an opportunity to earn better incomes without expanding agricultural activity into the gorillas' habitat. The coffee is then marketed to consumers who can support conservation through their purchases, with the initiative also contributing to CTPH's wider work.It is a thoughtful example of how wildlife protection need not come at the expense of local livelihoods. articles.summary: Few holiday campaigns keep the same faces on screen for long, and Sofía Vergara is one of the exceptions. It has been 15 years since she joined the St.
articles.body: Few holiday campaigns keep the same faces on screen for long, and Sofía Vergara is one of the exceptions. It has been 15 years since she joined the St. Jude Thanks and Giving campaign, which is now in its 23rd year. She returns alongside Drew Barrymore, Luis Fonsi, Jon Hamm and Michael Strahan, all longtime supporters who are encouraging people to give through online donations and in-store purchases. The annual holiday fundraising initiative supports St. Jude Children’s Research Hospital by raising funds for childhood cancer research and cures, as well as other life-threatening diseases. It also provides medical care to children battling these illnesses and supports patients and their families throughout the recovery process.How Sofía Vergara supports the causeActress Sofía Vergara has supported the holiday campaign for 15 years and is returning for its October 2026 launch. She calls it an honour to be part of the campaign. “St. Jude Children’s Research Hospital continues to inspire me year after year, and I'm honoured to support the St. Jude Thanks and Giving campaign for the 15th year,” the Modern Family actress said in a statement.She also spoke about the impressive work carried out by the hospital. “What makes St. Jude so extraordinary is that the discoveries made here are shared to help improve care for children around the world. I'm proud to support an organisation whose impact extends far beyond its campus and reaches families across the globe.”Filming alongside patientsFor this year’s campaign, the celebrity ambassadors filmed their holiday spots alongside St. Jude patients, which the hospital says gives the campaign a more personal connection. Drew Barrymore spent time with a patient named Nova and described the experience as inspiring. "I'm honoured to support St. Jude and the incredible work it does for children facing cancer and other life-threatening diseases. Spending time with Nova and seeing her joy and determination was truly inspiring. Supporting St. Jude means helping more children pursue their dreams and create lasting memories with the people they love,” she said in a statement.Luis Fonsi said being part of the campaign constantly reminds him why the mission is crucial. He was joined by Valentina, a patient, and said her courage and smile were unforgettable. “After many years supporting St. Jude, every visit reminds me why this mission matters. It was so meaningful to visit St. Jude this year and meet patients and their families, including Valentina, who joined me in my campaign spot. Her courage and smile were unforgettable. Children like Valentina show the importance of the lifesaving research, treatment and care, and the hope St. Jude gives to families facing childhood cancer and other life-threatening diseases."Michael Strahan also shared his experience of meeting patients and praised their resilience and positivity. “For the past 15 years, I’ve proudly supported St. Jude because of the meaningful difference it makes for children and their families. This year, I had the opportunity to spend time with Dominic, Brooke and Nico, and their resilience and positivity truly inspired me. I’m honoured to support St. Jude, a place that provides exceptional care and hope to families while giving kids the opportunity to focus on what matters most: being kids.”Jon Hamm spoke about paediatric research and what keeps him committed to it. "What impresses me the most about St. Jude is its commitment to continually moving paediatric research forward. Every breakthrough brings new hope for children facing cancer and other life-threatening diseases. I am proud to support this important work and help raise awareness for St. Jude to support children and their families."Ike Anand, president and CEO of ALSAC, St. Jude’s fundraising and awareness organisation, said the annual campaign gives children and families facing serious challenges more opportunities for hope, healing and time together. “The greatest gift is time, and participation in the St. Jude Thanks and Giving campaign helps give children and families facing some of life's toughest challenges more opportunities for hope, healing and more moments together. For 23 years, this campaign has united supporters around a shared purpose of helping St. Jude accelerate research and treatment so more children can reach milestones, make memories and look forward to a bright future.”Donations to the research hospital come through two channels: online gifts and purchases of limited-edition products at participating retailers. The brand roster is broad. Domino’s, Chili’s Grill & Bar, Dollar General, AutoZone, Williams Sonoma, J.Crew Factory, Kia, Zales and Jared all take part, along with KAY, HomeGoods and Homesense. Each brand brings its own customers into the effort. The biggest new name is Target, which rejoins the campaign for the first time since 2013. The retailer has worked with St. Jude for nearly 30 years.St. Jude Children’s Research Hospital opened in 1962, when childhood cancer was considered largely incurable. The hospital says it has since helped increase the overall survival rate in the United States from 20% to more than 80%.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: ‘That stops when I’m governor’: Texas governor-elect Gina Hinojosa warns Elon Musk, Big Tech over data centres
articles.summary: Texas governor-elect Gina Hinojosa has warned major technology companies, including Elon Musk’s businesses, that they will no longer be allowed to operate
articles.body: Texas governor-elect Gina Hinojosa has warned major technology companies, including Elon Musk’s businesses, that they will no longer be allowed to operate in the state without safeguards for local communities, saying their practice of taking advantage of Texans “stops when I’m governor”.In an interview with CNN, Hinojosa said data centres had expanded in largely rural parts of Texas without adequate regulations, leaving residents vulnerable to the impact of these projects.“Right now, what has happened is data centres have moved into mostly rural communities, and there are no rules and laws to protect Texans, and Texans are being taken advantage of,” she said.Hinojosa, who defeated Republican incumbent Greg Abbott in the November 3 election, said she was not opposed to data centres or the technology industry but wanted companies to work with communities rather than impose projects on them.“Is not that I hate data centres. I hate the way they are taking advantage of Texas. And that stops when I’m governor,” she said.She added that Texas could continue to attract businesses while ensuring that residents were protected. “We have always been a pro-business state in Texas, but what changes now with me as governor is it has to be a partnership that benefits Texans,” she said.Hinojosa has called for an immediate moratorium on new data-centre projects until state lawmakers put safeguards in place. She has also urged Abbott to issue an executive order halting construction before she takes office.The governor-elect said local communities must have a say in deciding whether data centres should be built in their areas and under what conditions. She told CNN that different parts of Texas had different needs and that residents should be able to walk away from negotiations if companies did not meet their demands.Hinojosa says relationship with Musk must be on Texas' termsHinojosa also addressed her potential relationship with Musk, whose companies SpaceX and Tesla have major operations in Texas.Asked whether Musk could move his businesses out of the state, she said she was open to working with him but insisted that companies would have to respect the interests of Texans.“We can have a strong working relationship with Musk and his companies, but it has to be on our terms. It cannot be just running over the people of Texas,” she said.Musk had backed Abbott and supported Republican candidates during the election campaign. He also spent heavily to promote Republican US Senate candidate Ken Paxton, who lost to Democrat James Talarico.The interview also touched on the proposed sale of a Texas state park near SpaceX's operations at Boca Chica to the company. Asked whether she would block the sale even if Musk considered moving his operations elsewhere, Hinojosa said the state needed to protect public access to its beaches.“Selling our beach to Elon Musk is just something that is almost unimaginable,” she said, calling the proposal “unacceptable”.She added that Texas beaches were constitutionally protected as public spaces and should remain accessible to residents.Hinojosa's victory ended more than three decades of Republican control of the Texas governor's office. She is set to become the state's first Democratic governor since Ann Richards left office in 1995 and its first Latina governor.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.
