articles.title: 10 years of the Paris Agreement, who are the top 10 carbon emitters of the world and where does India stand
articles.summary: Natural disasters, including the recent floods in Nepal and wildfires in Europe, have raised awareness about the impacts of climate change.
articles.body: Natural disasters, including the recent floods in Nepal and wildfires in Europe, have raised awareness about the impacts of climate change. According to the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC), “human activities, principally through emissions of greenhouse gases, have unequivocally caused global warming”, which is increasing the risks of extreme weather events. The Paris Agreement, adopted in 2015, set a global goal to limit this warming to well below 2°C and pursue efforts to keep it below 1.5°C.A decade later, measuring carbon emissions helps us understand the efforts taken by nations towards a clean energy transition. They tell the story of how the energy landscape has been transforming, yet how emissions remain at record highs. According to the 2025 Global Carbon Budget, global fossil-fuel CO₂ emissions are expected to reach a record high of approximately 38.1 billion tonnes in 2025. That's an enormous amount of carbon dioxide entering the atmosphere in just one year, largely from burning coal, oil and natural gas.But which countries are contributing the most? And where does India, one of the world's fastest-growing major economies, feature on this list?The world's 10 biggest carbon emittersThe following ranking focuses on annual fossil-fuel and industrial CO₂ emissions in 2024, the latest consolidated country-level data presented in the Global Carbon Budget 2025. These figures do not include all greenhouse gases or emissions from land-use change.China – 31.8%China has topped the list, accounting for nearly one-third of global fossil CO₂ emissions. Being a major industrialised economy, its enormous manufacturing industry, coal-powered electricity generation, steel production and construction sector all contribute to its carbon footprint. From producing electronics and machinery to building cities at breathtaking speed, China's industries consume huge amounts of energy.United States – 12.7%The United States contributes roughly one-eighth of global fossil CO₂ emissions. Its car-focused lifestyle, extensive road networks, aviation and industrial capacity are responsible for this huge contribution. Moreover, oil and natural gas remain major contributors.India – 8.3%India contributes around 8.3% of global fossil CO₂ emissions. With a population exceeding 1.4 billion, growing cities and expanding industries, there is increasing demand for electricity. While there has been an increase in energy from non-fossil fuel sources, coal remains a major part of the energy mix.Russia – 4.6%Russia's large oil and gas industry, along with its other energy-intensive industries, contributes significantly to its emissions. Industrial production, power generation and domestic heating, particularly because of its extremely cold climate, add to its carbon footprint.Japan – 2.5%Japan's position reflects its advanced industrial economy, manufacturing sector and considerable energy requirements. Cars, electronics, steel and chemical production all require energy.Indonesia – 2.1%Indonesia's emissions are driven by coal-powered electricity, industrial expansion and energy demand from its growing population. Indonesia is an island nation where its carbon footprint is also significantly influenced by land-use change and deforestation. These land-related emissions are counted separately from the fossil-fuel ranking discussed here.Iran – 2.0%Iran's large oil and natural gas industry is a major source of its carbon emissions. Domestic energy consumption, power generation and industrial activity add to the numbers. Its substantial fossil-fuel resources make transitioning towards cleaner energy a particularly important challenge.Saudi Arabia – 1.8%Saudi Arabia is one of the world's largest oil-producing nations. Along with emissions from the production and consumption of oil, other energy-intensive activities, including air conditioning and desalination, contribute significantly to the country's carbon footprint. These activities are particularly important given its desert climate.South Korea – 1.5%South Korea may be relatively small geographically, but its industrial footprint is considerable. With the majority of its industries operating in sectors such as electronics, shipbuilding, automobiles, steel and petrochemicals, the country requires substantial amounts of energy. Its continued reliance on fossil fuels, particularly coal and natural gas, makes decarbonising its industrial sector a major priority.Germany – approximately 1.5%Germany is an industrial nation with significant contributions to global supply chains for major industrial goods. Its enormous automotive industry and electricity generation are major contributors to its carbon footprint.Where does India really stand?Though India remains among the top three carbon emitters, its per-capita contributions remain considerably lower than those of other countries on the list.According to the Global Carbon Budget 2025, India's fossil CO₂ emissions per capita in 2024 were approximately 2.2 tonnes. Compare that with around 8.7 tonnes in China and 14.2 tonnes in the United States. In other words, India's overall emissions are high partly because of its enormous population, but the average Indian's carbon footprint remains considerably lower than that of people in these two countries.Moreover, India's fossil CO₂ emissions increased by 4% in 2024, the fastest growth among the four largest emitting countries in that year's Global Carbon Budget assessment. For 2025, the report projects a further 1.1% increase. The challenge is balancing economic development with environmental responsibility. Millions of people still need better access to electricity, transport, housing and other essentials.Ten years of the Paris Agreement: Has the world kept its promises?The Paris Agreement was a landmark moment in international climate diplomacy. The agreement was adopted on December 12, 2015, and entered into force on November 4, 2016. It provides a flexible approach, allowing each country to decide its own climate goals. This happens through the mechanism of Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs), which countries are required to submit and update every five years.Though there is increasing investment in renewable energy across several major economies, rising energy demand continues to offset much of this progress. The Global Carbon Budget 2025 estimates that coal accounted for approximately 41% of global fossil CO₂ emissions in 2024. This was followed by oil at 32% and natural gas at 21%. This reflects that, despite the growing availability of renewable energy, the world is still heavily dependent on fossil fuels.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.summary: Videos and photos show tear gas and fires throughout Paris as 70,000 security forces deploy against France protests despite police bans on gatherings.
articles.body: Protesters in France are continuing to demonstrate in Paris and across the nation despite police prohibitions on gatherings in the capital. The Paris Police Prefecture denied numerous formal requests for permits allowing protests in various areas of the city, citing October riots that led to thousands of arrests and violent clashes between protesters and law enforcement. "These events demonstrated the intention of certain individuals to target the institutions of the Republic, specifically through actions directed against public buildings and State services in order to undermine the foundations of the Republic," the police wrote, according to a Fox News Digital translation of a police order. "That these elements characterize a particular and serious risk to public institutions, agent safety, and the normal functioning of public services during such demonstrations," the statement continued. FRANCE'S MACRON BLAMES PROTESTS ON 'ULTRA-LEFT GROUPS WHOSE AIM IS TO BRING DOWN THE REPUBLIC' FRANCE DEPLOYS 70,000 POLICE OFFICERS TO PREPARE FOR NEW WAVE OF PROTESTS ON HALLOWEEN Police also prohibited a rally of France's popular Yellow Vest protest movement scheduled for Place de la Concorde, citing security concerns. Despite the ban, prominent Yellow Vest members attended and were arrested at the National Assembly in front of Place de la Concorde. Benjamin Ball, a member of the Yellow Vests coordination group, and spokesperson Azelma Sigaux, were both arrested early in the afternoon Saturday, according to the Agence France-Presse (AFP). PHOTOS SHOW AFTERMATH OF RIOTS AS MASKED GROUPS CLASH WITH POLICE ACROSS FRANCE France's Interior Ministry anticipated 170,000 people to protest nationwide Saturday, a day marking the fourth straight week of protests. The country deployed 70,000 security forces to quell the demonstrations, according to the AFP. "The risk is exactly the same as on previous Saturdays," Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said, instructing authorities "not to lower their guard," AFP reported. LIMOGES TOWN HALL 'LARGELY LOST' AFTER FAR-LEFT RIOTERS SET HISTORIC BUILDING ON FIRE AMID FRENCH UNREST Videos and photos showed French authorities deploying tear gas and detaining rioters while fires burned throughout Paris. French authorities also report that protesters have lobbed projectiles at police. Demonstrators are protesting high costs of living, among other things, as student and teacher unions join Yellow Vests at the mass rallies. On Monday, French Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu is due to meet with leaders from the unions to discuss wages and purchasing power, AFP reported. Despite the planned tête-à-tête, union leaders are calling for fresh strikes on Tuesday to keep the pressure on the government, claiming the unions are "in a position of strength (and) the government in a position of weakness and starting to yield." articles.body: US President Donald Trump has offered Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC) chief executive Dana White the job of White House press secretary, urging his longtime friend and political ally to accept the position. The offer comes after the departure of Karoline Leavitt and the exceptionally brief tenure of her successor, Katie Zacharia.Trump announced the offer in a post on his Truth Social platform on Saturday, November 7, describing White as a “violent Fighter and Warrior”.The president also suggested that White bring several UFC fighters to the White House as his assistants, naming Islam Makhachev, Khabib Nurmagomedov, Justin Gaethje, Daniel Cormier, Amanda Nunes and Kayla Harrison.“We need these people to defend us against the Lunatic Left. Dana will be a Press Secretary like none other. Dana, please take the job!” Trump wrote.It was not immediately clear whether White would accept the offer. Trump did not provide details about when White might take up the position.What happened to Karoline Leavitt?Leavitt was the first press secretary of Trump's second administration, taking up the position when he returned to the White House in January 2025. She announced her departure in August 2026, after the birth of her second child in May. Leavitt said she wanted to spend more time with her family. She left the White House on August 27 and subsequently joined Fox News as a contributor.Katie Zacharia's five-day stintTrump announced on October 9 that Katie Zacharia, then a senior communications adviser at Trump Media & Technology Group, would replace Leavitt. Zacharia had previously worked in the Department of Homeland Security's public affairs office and appeared as a conservative commentator on Fox News and Newsmax. She had also been involved in Trump's political campaigns.However, her tenure lasted only five days. She began work on October 12 and was out by October 16, after delivering just one press briefing.Reports said Trump had urged her to reconsider the position following criticism of her first briefing and questions about her professional credentials. Trump said he was in no hurry to appoint another press secretary.Who is Dana White?White, 56, has been the face of the UFC since taking over as its president in 2001. He helped turn mixed martial arts into a global sporting phenomenon and is known for his outspoken personality. He has been a longtime supporter and friend of Trump, appearing at Republican political events and speaking at the Republican National Convention. Trump has also regularly attended UFC events.White's possible move to the White House would be a major departure from his career in sports promotion. The press secretary is responsible for communicating the administration's positions, answering questions from journalists and defending the president's policies. Trump's public offer, however, does not amount to a confirmed appointment. White has yet to publicly say whether he intends to take the job.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: Trump orders DOJ to investigate Democrats for ‘threatening’ people
articles.summary: Trump lashed out at Democrats on Truth Social days after the party won control of Congress.
articles.body:
United States President Donald Trump has ordered the ⁠⁠Department of Justice (DOJ) to look into Democrats ‌‌for “threatening a lot of people” with impeachment and other ⁠⁠forms of ⁠⁠punishment, following their midterm election victory.

In a Truth Social post on Saturday, Trump said what Democrats had done amounted to a “criminal act”, without providing evidence.

The post comes days after Democrats won control of both chambers of the US Congress from Republicans in Tuesday’s midterm elections . Democratic lawmakers and newly elected candidates have said they would pursue probes into the Trump family’s financial dealings, US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), as well as investigations into Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth and Attorney General Todd Blanche.

“The Democrats are going around threatening a lot of people,” Trump wrote, adding that some of his cabinet have been threatened with impeachment. “This is extortion at the highest level, and they should be held accountable for this.”

Trump also said, without evidence, that some Democrats were threatening his donors, whom he called “some of the most respected people anywhere in the World”. He said Democrats were targeting them for their political views, specifically calling out Michigan Senator Elissa Slotkin. He gave no evidence of her threatening people over their views.

When Democrats take control of Congress in January, they will be able to conduct a range of investigations, in which they can order access to documents, summon Trump officials to testify, and hold hearings.

Democratic Representative Robert Garcia of California, who is likely to chair the powerful House Oversight Committee, which serves as the investigative committee in the House and has broad jurisdiction and power, posted “LAWYER UP” on social media after it was clear Democrats would take the House.

During his second term, Trump has called for investigations into his political enemies, including the former director of the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), James Comey , and New York Attorney General Letitia James.

articles.title: Israeli president Herzog picks Netanyahu's rival Gadi Eisenkot to form next government
articles.summary: Israeli President Isaac Herzog on Saturday tasked opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot with forming the next government, giving Prime Minister Benjamin
articles.body: Israeli President Isaac Herzog on Saturday tasked opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot with forming the next government, giving Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s main challenger the first opportunity to assemble a coalition after the October 27 election produced no clear parliamentary majority.Eisenkot, a former military chief and head of the Yashar party, secured the backing of representatives from parties accounting for 67 lawmakers during consultations with Herzog. Netanyahu, whose Likud party emerged as the largest in parliament with 27 seats, received recommendations from factions representing 46 lawmakers. His broader bloc holds 53 seats in the 120-member Knesset, while Eisenkot’s opposition bloc has 48. A majority requires 61 seats.The announcement came shortly after Netanyahu called for a “national unity government” in a video statement, urging the formation of an alliance among Zionist political factions. He also warned against “hastily swearing in a government with terrorist supporters” — an apparent reference to the Arab-led parties.Netanyahu has argued that a broad alliance is needed to protect Israel and confront regional threats, particularly Iran. He said such a government would “permanently remove the nuclear threat from Iran, preserve Israel as a Jewish state, and bring unity among us,” according to Al Jazeera.The opposition rejected the appeal. Democratic Party chairman Yair Golan said, “Netanyahu’s government must be replaced, and a government of salvation and change must be formed to safeguard Israel’s democracy, security, and future. We are committed to making every effort to make this happen,” he posted on X.Eisenkot’s path to power, however, remains complicated. One option is a minority government backed by the two Arab-led parties, Ra’am and the Joint List, which together hold 19 seats. Both have indicated willingness to support an alternative government, but several of Eisenkot’s potential partners have ruled out relying on Arab parties.Another possibility is an agreement with ultra-Orthodox factions holding 13 seats. That would require difficult negotiations over exemptions from military service for ultra-Orthodox seminary students, an issue Eisenkot and some of his partners have pledged to address.A unity arrangement with Likud is also mathematically possible, although it would require major political compromises from both sides.Herzog’s decision gives Eisenkot 28 days to negotiate a coalition, with a possible two-week extension. If he fails, Netanyahu could be given an opportunity to form a government. Should successive attempts prove unsuccessful, Israel could face another election, prolonging the political uncertainty.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: In 2015, an Arkansas couple began buying 111 acres on instalments, later handing over a truck and cows to catch up; when the seller resisted closing, an appeals court upheld their right to complete the sale
articles.summary: A land purchase can stretch across years, with missed payments, revised agreements and disputes over who has the right to sell the property.
articles.body: A land purchase can stretch across years, with missed payments, revised agreements and disputes over who has the right to sell the property. In Arkansas, a couple who began paying for 111 acres in 2015 faced a legal battle after the seller refused to provide the signed paperwork needed to complete the purchase. Destin later testified that the couple had handed over a truck and six or seven cows under an earlier arrangement to bring their payments up to date. On November 4, 2026, the Arkansas Court of Appeals upheld their right to complete the sale, affirming a ruling that recognised their equitable interest in the land.In its decision in Sandra Thomas v. Destin and Jennifer Clark, case number CV-25-445, the court affirmed the Logan County Circuit Court's order for specific performance. The opinion, available on Justia, also upheld an award of $17,500 in attorney's fees and costs to the buyers, Destin and Jennifer Clark.How the couple's land purchase beganThe dispute concerned 111 acres in Magazine, Arkansas, owned by George Wayne Thomas and his wife, Sandra Thomas. Destin Clark testified that he first discussed buying the property with George in 2015, when owner financing was presented as a possibility. Under the initial arrangement, the Clarks were to pay $2,700 a month, but they fell behind and were told to leave.After struggling to find another place to live, the couple asked the Thomases to let them restart the agreement. Destin told the court that they handed over a truck and six or seven cows to bring the outstanding balance up to date and agreed again to pay $2,700 each month. They later defaulted a second time.On March 3, 2020, the parties entered into a third agreement titled “Rent To Own Contract”. This time, the monthly payment was set at $1,900, with the outstanding balance listed as $103,852.91. The contract allowed the buyers to make advance payments towards part or all of the debt without a penalty. It also stated that ownership would remain with the sellers until the balance was paid.Disagreement over the final paymentBy 2021, the Thomases were urging the Clarks to clear the remaining debt. The couple wanted to buy property in Kentucky and planned to sell the Arkansas acreage to fund that purchase. In February 2022, they received an offer of $240,700 for the land.To move the transaction forward, the title company required a dated and signed payoff figure from the sellers. Destin asked Sandra for the amount in writing, but she said the Clarks could not sell the property without the Thomases' express written permission.The couple received another offer in April 2022, this time for $250,000. Sandra told Destin that the payoff amount was $73,410 as of April 15. He accepted the figure but again requested a signed document. The court record showed that the paperwork was not provided.The payment dispute added to the conflict. The Clarks sent cashier's checks for an instalment due on April 15, along with $440 in late fees, but the envelope arrived 46 days after the due date and was marked “Refused”. Sandra later issued a notice requiring the couple to leave, citing late payments and alleged failure to maintain the property.Why the courts upheld the buyers' rightsThe Clarks sued the Thomases, seeking enforcement of the agreement and the right to complete the purchase. The circuit court found that the 2020 contract created an equitable mortgage and that the couple had acquired an equitable interest in the property. It also concluded that Sandra had breached the agreement by refusing to provide the signed payoff figure after the buyers had sought to make an early payment.On appeal, Sandra argued that the agreement was only an executory contract, meaning the Clarks had no equitable ownership before completing all its conditions. She also challenged the findings concerning late payments, the property's condition and the attorney's fees.The appeals court disagreed with her central argument. It noted that Arkansas law allows courts to consider how parties have acted while carrying out a land agreement, not just the wording of the document. It also stressed that the Clarks had paid a significant amount towards the purchase since early 2015 and that equity generally seeks to prevent harsh forfeitures.The court concluded that the trial judge had not clearly erred in ordering specific performance. Under that order, Sandra had to provide a signed payoff amount calculated from $73,410, with interest at six per cent annually from April 15, 2022. The Clarks were then required to arrange closing within 30 days of receiving it, while Sandra had to accept the final payment and execute the deed.Appeals court leaves the order intactThe Arkansas Court of Appeals affirmed the lower court's decision, including the $17,500 award for attorney's fees and costs. articles.title: Veterans shouldn't sleep rough this Christmas, Burnham says
articles.summary: Downing Street says the prime minister will personally write to councils on Armistice Day to urge them to draw up plans.
articles.body:
No one who served in the UK armed forces should have to sleep on the streets this Christmas, Andy Burnham has said.

Downing Street said the prime minister will personally write to councils across England on Armistice Day (11 November) to urge them to draw up specific plans to offer accommodation for veterans sleeping rough ahead of the festive period.

He will say that, going forward, national and local government should work under the "simple principle" that "no one who has served our country should ever be left to sleep rough on our streets".

Burnham will ask local authorities to use part of the additional £874m already announced to tackle homelessness specifically for housing veterans.

"People who stepped forward prepared to put their lives on the line for the rest of us should never lack a roof over their head," Burnham said in a statement issued on Saturday.

"When they need help, the country owes them more than warm words. It owes them a bed every night, a proper plan and someone in their corner from day one."

The PM will ask councils to work with local organisations and charities to tackle homelessness amongst veterans.

Downing Street said an additional £8.7m in funding would be allocated to eight organisations across the UK to help housing providers offer assistance to veterans with complex needs, including those with health or addiction problems.

Among them are Veteran Housing Scotland, Launchpad and SSAFA, the Armed Forces Charity.

The pledge, announced ahead of Remembrance Sunday, is part of Burnham's wider plan to offer everyone currently sleeping rough a bed this winter.

The most recent official figures estimated that there were 4,793 people sleeping rough on a single night in autumn 2025 in England - a record high. The number of people recorded as sleeping rough has been on the rise since 2021.

The government has committed £4.4bn in total to end rough sleeping.

Burnham previously faced criticism from the Conservatives for failing to end rough sleeping while he was the mayor of Greater Manchester.

He argued that Manchester's scheme attracted rough sleepers from the surrounding regions, adding that "it's only if everywhere does it at the same level that you can actually end rough sleeping".

Liberal Democrats defence spokesman James MacCleary MP said the funding was an "important first step" but that "a one-off cash injection won't fix a crisis years in the making".

He urged Burnham to guarantee long-term funding for councils to tackle homelessness "for good" and to put in place measures to prevent veterans "falling through the cracks in the first place".

The prime minister is urging any veterans who are sleeping rough, or those supporting them, to call a UK-wide helpline on 0800 9520774 to be connected directly to housing and other specialist support.

articles.title: Israel’s president picks Eisenkot over Netanyahu to form next government
articles.summary: Isaac Herzog formally gives Gadi Eisenkot 28 days to secure 61 Knesset seats and replace Netanyahu as prime minister.
articles.body:
Israel’s President Isaac Herzog has tasked Gadi Eisenkot with forming the country’s next government, passing over the former army chief’s rival, Benjamin Netanyahu.

Herzog told Eisenkot of his decision on Saturday evening and will formally hand him the mandate at a ceremony on Sunday, the president’s spokesperson said.

Herzog held consultations with political parties this week to decide who he would appoint to form a government after neither side secured a majority in the October 27 general election.

Some 67 lawmakers, including from Arab-led parties, endorsed Eisenkot, leader of the Yashar party, to form the next government, while only 46 backed Netanyahu, the current prime minister.

Eisenkot will have 28 days – with a possible 14-day extension – to build a coalition of at least 61 of the Knesset’s 120 seats, the minimum threshold for a government.

In the October election, Eisenkot’s four-party alliance won 48 seats, while Netanyahu’s right-wing and religious bloc secured 53, leaving both short of the 61 needed for a parliamentary majority. Arab-led parties, representing Palestinian citizens of Israel, won a record 19 seats.

Eisenkot has ruled out forming a government with the Arab-led parties, which would give him a 67-seat bloc. Winning over the two ultra-Orthodox parties, United Torah Judaism and Shas, would give him exactly 61 seats.

He could also form a government with fewer than 61 seats if he wins a parliamentary confidence vote.

Al Jazeera’s Nour Odeh, reporting from Ramallah in the occupied West Bank on Herzog’s decision, said the president “took the predictable route” in selecting Eisenkot, as he had the highest number of recommendations.

“The hard work will begin now for Eisenkot to put together a government that can pass a vote of confidence at the Knesset that: one, will not break too many of the promises he made on the campaign trail; and two, that can survive the opposition of the right-wing bloc led by Netanyahu,” Odeh said.

If Eisenkot fails to form a government within the allotted time, Herzog will nominate another candidate. If the second nominee fails, a parliament majority can back a third candidate, who will be granted a final 14 days.

If, once again, no government is formed, a new election will be called within 90 days, with Netanyahu staying on as a caretaker prime minister.

Eisenkot led Israel’s military from 2015 to 2019 and sat as an observer in Netanyahu’s war cabinet for the first eight months of Israel’s genocidal war on Gaza, which began in October 2023.

Ahmad Tibi, a senior member of the Joint List – a coalition of Arab-led parties that holds 11 seats – told Al Jazeera on Saturday that Herzog’s decision was “expected”.

“We were concerned that the president would move towards a national unity government,” he said, referring to a proposed power-sharing agreement between Eisenkot and Netanyahu.

Instead, Arab-led parties endorsed Eisenkot for the mandate, granting him a “considerable margin”.

Tibi said he believes Eisenkot is headed for a minority government “with external support from the Arab parties”.

While this would not be a “dream government” for Arab-led parties, Tibi prioritised bringing down “the government of Netanyahu, [Itamar] Ben-Gvir and [Bezalel] Smotrich”.

Hours before Herzog’s decision, Netanyahu had warned that a government formed by the opposition bloc with support from Arab-led parties would lead to Israel’s collapse.

“Such a government, dependent on Islamists, will dismantle the state of Israel from within, as is happening in European countries, and far worse than that,” Netanyahu said in a prerecorded video speech, echoing the language of far-right politicians who falsely claim parts of Europe have come under Islamic law.

Netanyahu “described us as supporters of terrorists and terrorism”, Tibi said. “My response to him is this: Netanyahu is the biggest terrorist in Israel and the region, and the foremost supporter of terrorism, particularly Jewish terrorism in the West Bank and the Palestinian territories.”

Al Jazeera’s Odeh noted that although Eisenkot has expressly said he does not wish to form a government with Arab-led parties, “they both share quite compelling reasons to get rid of Netanyahu”.

articles.title: Israel’s president taps opposition candidate Eisenkot to form a government, in setback for Netanyahu
articles.summary: Israeli President Isaac Herzog said Saturday night that he was giving opposition candidate Gadi Eisenkot the first opportunity to form a governing coalition following elections on Oct. 27.
articles.body: JERUSALEM — Israeli President Isaac Herzog said Saturday night that he was giving opposition candidate Gadi Eisenkot the first opportunity to form a governing coalition following elections on Oct. 27. Eisenkot, a former military chief, ran as the main challenger to Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, leading a bloc of parties seeking to oust Israel’s longest-serving premier. Neither Eisenkot nor Netanyahu won a clear majority in the vote. But in marathon discussions with the president this week, representatives from most of Israel’s main parties recommended Eisenkot be tasked with assembling a new government. The announcement, which had been expected on Sunday, came shortly after Netanyahu called for a “national unity government” in a video statement and warned against “hastily swearing in a government with terrorist supporters” – an apparent reference to the Arab-led parties. Netanyahu and his allies have repeatedly portrayed the Arab-led parties as a threat to national security, while Eisenkot has indicated a willingness to partner with them under certain conditions, including calling Hamas a terrorist group that needs to be destroyed. Eisenkot’s party, Yashar, slammed the prime minister’s video with a statement posted on X and urged members of his party, Likud, to disavow their alliance with “radical parties,” in an apparent reference to the more extreme parties in his religious-nationalist base. The statement argued that Eisenkot would only include parties and parliament members who support its principles, including recognizing Hamas as a terrorist organization.

Donald Robert Morris-Jones, 76, was driving on Optimist Farm Road in Wake County Saturday morning when he crossed the center line and struck the group of cyclists, the North Carolina State Highway Patrol said. The incident unfolded about 14 miles southwest of Raleigh. After striking the group, the vehicle traveled away from the scene then ran off the left side of the roadway and crashed into a ditch a half a mile away from the cyclists, officials said. The North Carolina State Highway Patrol responded to the scene just after 9:30 a.m. One cyclist died as a result of the crash and at least a dozen more were hurt, authorities said. Their injuries range from minor to serious, and several were transported to hospitals for treatment. Morris-Jones was taken into custody and booked on a charge of driving while impaired, according to Wake County Sheriff’s Office inmate records. “Impairment is suspected to be a factor in the crash,” the agency said.

articles.title: Poland mass shooting: PM says footage shows 3 bodies at suspect’s home; minister cites far-right influence
articles.summary: Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk has referred to footage showing bodies at the home of the man suspected of carrying out a mass shooting in Krakow, as
articles.body: Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk has referred to footage showing bodies at the home of the man suspected of carrying out a mass shooting in Krakow, as investigators probe the background of an attack that left six people dead and 15 injured.Speaking at a news conference on Sunday, the PM said three people, two women and a man, were found dead inside the home of the suspect, and were likely close members of his family. Tusk described the discovery late Saturday as “the next acts of this tragedy”.Meanwhile, interior minister Marcin Kierwiński said the 25-year-old suspect was influenced by far-right ideologies, describing his views as “very radical” and “ultranationalistic”.The attack took place on Saturday afternoon in Krakow’s Main Market Square, a major tourist hub in the heart of the Old Town. The suspect, a Polish citizen, drove through the crowded square and opened fire at multiple locations with an automatic weapon, authorities said. Police later shot and wounded him before taking him to hospital for surgery.The victims comprised four women and two men. At least three of the women were Polish, while one of those killed was a British citizen. Authorities were still working to identify the remaining two victims, officials said at a news conference.“Everything indicates that he was fascinated by far-right ideologies,” Kierwiński said, adding that the suspect held “very radical” views. The minister did not disclose the man’s identity.Poland’s defence minister Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz described the shooting as an “act of terror” against the people of Krakow. The city, Poland’s second-largest, receives around 15 million visitors a year, many of whom visit the Main Market Square.Krakow police spokesperson Katarzyna Cisło said the attacker wore military-style fatigues and a bulletproof vest and used a military-type long gun. Police found additional weapons and ammunition in his car. She said the suspect continued firing at officers even after being shot.Describing the attacker's movements through the square, Cisło said he went on a “wild ride”, resulting in people being wounded at several locations. She added that he appeared to have acted alone and that there was no continuing threat to the public.Two police officers were among the injured, one seriously, Kierwiński said. Police commander Marek Boroń said five foreign nationals were also wounded. Authorities said 13 of the injured were hospitalised in serious condition, although that figure may have included the suspect. Two people were treated and released within hours of the shooting.The attack also affected transport and the square’s horse-drawn carriage trade. Krakow’s municipal transport company said a tram driver reported that his vehicle had been shot at by a man in a moving car near the square, shattering the cabin window. Animal rights group OTOZ Animals said the attacker also shot two horses; both survived, though one was hit in the leg.Mayor Łukasz Gibała announced official mourning in Krakow until Wednesday. “The square will belong to us again,” he said in a video posted on X, while insisting the city would remain open to visitors.Tusk praised the police response, while president Karol Nawrocki expressed support for the victims, the wounded and their families.
